fixed_global_transition_model.name: FIXED_POINT_PLUS_ALL_FINITE_FIELD_LINEAR_ALGEBRAIC_OPERATORS
fixed_global_transition_model.semantics: The implicit global decision/progress language extends fixed-point logic by linear-algebraic operators acting on vector spaces over finite fields of all prime characteristics. This scope is intentionally broader than original FPR and includes uniform finite-field linear-algebraic access of the kind needed to avoid the fixed-prime defect isolated in R44AH.

published_theorem.title: Limitations of the invertible-map equivalences
published_theorem.statement_used: Combining CFI constructions over fields and over the rings Z_{2^i}, the authors prove that no fixed k makes the invertible-map equivalence using the set of all primes coincide with isomorphism on all finite graphs. They conclude that no extension of fixed-point logic by linear-algebraic operators over fields can capture polynomial time.
published_theorem.witness_type: Polynomial-time decidable isomorphism/CFI properties that remain invisible to the all-finite-field linear-algebraic logic.

derived_TRUMP_barrier.claim: Even an implicit global TRUMP semantic language equipped with the full family of finite-field linear-algebraic operators cannot be treated as a universal PTIME/exactness language for arbitrary finite constraint structures.
reason: R44AG showed FPC lacks even fixed-field affine solvability; R44AH showed original fixed-prime rank logic lacks uniform prime-parametrized rank.
The cited all-primes result goes beyond both defects: even allowing linear-algebraic operators over every finite-field characteristic still leaves polynomial-time properties outside the language.
Therefore finite-field linear algebra, even uniformly and globally available, is not by itself a universal L1/L2 semantic substrate.
The separating constructions use ring-valued CFI structure over Z_{2^i}, showing a concrete algebraic direction not reducible to vector-space operations over fields.

dead_zone_mapping.meaning: Uniform access to every finite field can still leave a semantic dead zone for polynomial-time structure living over finite rings/modules.

what_is_not_proved: No barrier is claimed for fixed-point languages additionally equipped with sufficiently general finite-ring/module operators unless separately proved.
No runtime lower bound is claimed for ordinary Turing-machine algorithms using finite-field or finite-ring computations.
No direct 3SAT hardness theorem follows from the descriptive-complexity separation.

TRUMP_architecture_consequence.rule: Do not identify 'global algebraic state' with 'finite-field rank/matrix state'. A universal implicit invariant must state exactly which algebraic domains and operators it supports and prove semantics preservation for arbitrary 3CNF transformations.

next_admissible_math.question: Does extending the fixed global model from finite fields to the specific finite-ring/module phenomena exposed by Z_{2^i} yield a known PTIME-capable but still non-universal logic, or is there a theorem barrier for an even more general algebraic-operator language?
forbidden: claiming rings solve 3SAT because fields are insufficient
transferring graph-isomorphism separation directly to SAT complexity
